  - heading "Privacy Policy" [level=1]
  - paragraph: "Last updated: June 2026"
  - paragraph: This Privacy Policy explains how Umrah Connect collects, uses and protects information across our platform — for travelers, operators, hotels, transport companies, visa agencies and finance teams.
  - heading "1. Information we collect" [level=2]
  - paragraph: We collect information you provide when you create an account, complete bookings, submit website forms, or contact us — such as your name, email, phone number, organization and travel details. For providers, we also collect business and KYC verification information.
  - heading "2. How we use your information" [level=2]
  - paragraph: "We use your information to operate the platform: to process bookings and payments, coordinate between travelers and providers, verify provider identity, send notifications, provide support, and improve our services. Operator and pilgrim data is scoped to its tenant."
  - heading "3. Data sharing" [level=2]
  - paragraph: We share booking and coordination data only with the providers and operators directly involved in your journey. We do not sell your personal information. Service providers who help us run the platform are bound by confidentiality obligations.
  - heading "4. Data security" [level=2]
  - paragraph: We protect your data with encrypted authentication, role-based access control, multi-tenant isolation and audit logging. Access to your data is restricted to your role and tenant.
  - heading "5. Data retention" [level=2]
  - paragraph: We retain your information for as long as your account is active or as needed to provide services, comply with legal obligations, resolve disputes and enforce agreements.
  - heading "6. Your rights" [level=2]
  - paragraph: You may request access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal information, subject to legal and operational requirements. Contact us to exercise these rights.
  - heading "7. Contact" [level=2]
  - paragraph: For privacy questions or requests, contact us through the Contact page. We will respond as promptly as we can.

    - heading "Best times to visit the Rawdah in Madinah" [level=1]
    - paragraph:
      - text: 4 min read · Umrah Connect team
    - paragraph: The Rawdah ash-Sharifah — the area between the Prophet’s ﷺ minbar and his blessed home — is one of the most sought-after places on earth. A little planning makes the visit calmer and more likely to succeed.
    - heading "Book through Nusuk first" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Entry to the Rawdah is organised through timed permits booked in the official Nusuk app. Permits are free but limited; slots open on a rolling basis, so check the app daily and book as soon as your travel dates are confirmed.
    - paragraph: Men and women have separate visiting hours and entrances — check which window your permit falls into and arrive early for it.
    - heading "The calmest windows" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Late night (after Isha crowds disperse, roughly 11pm–2am) and the period after Fajr are usually the most settled times. Between Dhuhr and Asr is often quieter than the evening rush.
    - paragraph: Fridays, the last ten nights of Ramadan and Hajj season are the busiest — if your trip allows, plan your Rawdah visit for a mid-week day outside peak season.
    - heading "On the day" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Arrive at the gate printed on your permit at least 20–30 minutes early, keep your Nusuk QR code ready offline, and travel light — large bags slow down entry.
    - paragraph: Once inside, time is short. Prioritise two rak‘ahs and your most important du‘ās rather than photography; guards keep the flow moving.
    - heading "For operators" [level=2]
    - paragraph: If you manage groups, collect your pilgrims’ Nusuk accounts early and coordinate permit slots per group. Staggering sub-groups across windows works better than pushing one large block into a single slot.

    - paragraph: "Saudi Arabia has consolidated Umrah journeys onto official platforms: Nusuk for pilgrims and Masar for licensed operators. Knowing which path applies to your travellers avoids most visa surprises."
    - heading "The two official rails" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "Nusuk is the pilgrim-facing platform — individuals can obtain an Umrah eVisa or book Rawdah permits directly. Masar is the operator rail: licensed agents register packages, pilgrims and services through it, and group visas flow against those records."
    - heading "Typical document set" [level=2]
    - paragraph: A passport valid 6+ months beyond travel, a clear passport-photo scan, completed vaccination requirements, and — for group files — consistent name spelling exactly as in the passport machine-readable zone. Mismatched transliterations are the single most common rejection cause.
    - heading "Timelines to plan around" [level=2]
    - paragraph: eVisas can issue quickly, but group files move at the speed of their slowest document. Operators should lock passports and photos at booking time, not at submission time, and track each pilgrim’s checklist so one missing scan doesn’t stall the file.
    - heading "How Umrah Connect helps" [level=2]
    - paragraph: The compliance workspace tracks each application’s status (draft → submitted → approved/rejected with reason), keeps the document checklist against the pilgrim record, and shows the pipeline per group. Direct regulator API integration is on the roadmap — today the platform organises the work; submission happens on the official portals.

    - heading "Invoices, payments and reconciliation" [level=1]
    - paragraph:
      - text: 5 min read · Umrah Connect team
    - paragraph: "Umrah finance fails quietly: a deposit here, a cash payment there, and by departure week nobody is sure who still owes what. The cure is deriving status from recorded payments — never the other way round."
    - heading "Invoice from the booking" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Generate the invoice directly from the booking so amounts, currency and the pilgrim list always match the operational record. Manual invoices drift; generated ones can’t.
    - heading "Record every payment, however small" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "Each deposit or instalment goes in with amount, method and reference. The invoice then derives its own state: Draft/Sent → Partially Paid → Paid when the running total reaches the invoice amount. Overpayments are rejected, so the ledger cannot go negative."
    - heading "Read the reconciliation, not the inbox" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "The Partial filter is your working list: every invoice there has money outstanding, with the exact remainder shown. Departure-readiness reviews become a five-minute scan instead of an archaeology dig."
    - heading "Refunds and cancellations" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Cancel or void invoices rather than deleting them, and record refunds against the original payment so the audit trail stays complete. Deleted history always comes back as a dispute.
